column1: # Retargets applied 2026-09-11 after the 09-10 design pass on Skai-Games: seven same-title rebuilds found by figma-drift.mjs plus seven role-matched pairs for the 347-wide mobile frames replaced by 375-wide ones.
# Each row restates the work carried from the old frame; a frame whose geometry changed is partial until re-measured. Columns: key, status, primaryFile, route, reason, bp.

column5: BEST-VERIFIED SECTION IN THE CASINO: 6 of 9 frames verified `match` against measured DOM, not by eye - board 9163-4529 (tile 103.047 vs Figma 103.0408, gap 11.437 vs 11.449, radius 5.152 and border 3.4347 exact, ring colours #FF574A bomb / #17F9B4 gem on a constant #001615 tile, the frame's 150%/135.48% BOMB_CROP rather than a plain cover, committed gem.png/bomb.png and one extracted tile-bolt.svg), mobile board 9163-6955 holding the identical 0.1111 gap/tile ratio, bet panel Advanced-off 9163-7155 (every label verbatim, Mines: is the frame's combobox and the DOM reports no input[type=range], CTA 324x52 #56C7F3 radius 16), Advanced-Auto 9163-7972 (all six advanced labels), and both mobile panel states 9163-8481 / 9163-8621 including the frame's CTA-above-toggle inversion. The 4 page frames stay `partial` for reasons already on record: 9003-110110 tablet A is the REJECTED rival of B (A's 708-wide letterbox board with Manual/Auto above the CTA contradicts both B and mobile, so only B's shape was built) and 9163-5572's own info-block title and card art read 'Dice' - designer leftovers deliberately not reproduced, along with its clipped Dice trio below the frame bottom. ★ 2026-08-05 - BOTH previously-recorded wrong controls are now CLEARED, and the Potential Profit number was wrong TWICE for two different reasons. (1a) EDGE, fixed earlier (2cc8e0e): MinesGame.tsx floored at *98 (2%) against the rail's MINES_EDGE_BPS=9500 (_shared/mines.ts:126), quoting 1.46x where 1.4188x settles. (1b) ROUNDING, fixed now: the corrected client still floored to TWO DECIMALS (`Math.floor(mult * 95) / 100`) while the rail floors to ONE BPS (_shared/mines.ts:279-281, exact BigInt `Number(num / den)`), so 3 mines / 3 reveals printed 1.41x against a settled 1.4188x - low, never high, so no player was shortchanged, but still a number the rail contradicts. MinesGame.tsx:144-148 and MinefieldPro.tsx:120-121 now both delegate to a new pure module minesOdds.ts, a port of the rail's BigInt ladder rather than a second derivation of it, and minesOdds.test.ts pins it to bps values LIFTED FROM PRODUCTION points_game_rounds rows (10795 at 3 mines/1 reveal, 12337 at 3/2, 14188 at 3/3, 19166 at 3/5, 11875 at 5/1, 15000 at 5/2, 980448 at 6/12 where a 1000-point stake paid 98044) plus a source-text guard on MINES_EDGE_BPS / MINES_TILES in the edge function - an oracle the client cannot satisfy by agreeing with itself. The same pass floored the PAYOUT surfaces the integer POINTS rail floors: potentialProfit and the `Cash Out N` CTA both route through minesPayout(), because fmtAmount rounds POINTS half-up and a raw 10.795 printed 'Cash Out 11' against a settlement of 10. (2) GRID SIZE is honest rather than wired, and that is deliberate: the rail genuinely cannot take it. _shared/mines.ts hardcodes MINES_TILES=25 into the Pascal table, the Fisher-Yates board, the tile-range validation and the ladder; points-game mines_start (index.ts:3840-3860) accepts betAmount/mineCount/clientSeed and NO gridSize; pointsGameService.startPointsMines has no such parameter and gameSettlementService.ts:1624-1631 drops the field. minesTheme.LIVE_RAIL_GRID_SIZES=[25] now gates the control - all four design segments still render, 36/49/Custom are DISABLED with the reason on the control, and the pre-bet quote can no longer price a 64-tile ladder the server settles as 25. Widening it is an engine change plus an edge-function deploy, not a UI change; widen LIVE_RAIL_GRID_SIZES the day the engine takes a board size. ★ 2026-08-05 - THE GRID GATE IS NOW VERIFIED IN A BROWSER, AND THE SECOND SELECTOR IS CLOSED TOO. /play/mines loaded and the four segments read from the live DOM: 25 enabled, 36 and 49 disabled carrying the title "36-tile boards are not supported by the settlement engine yet", Custom disabled with "No custom board sizes are available". So the honest-control claim above is confirmed by measurement, not by reading the source. ★ CORRECTION to the line this replaces: MinefieldPro.tsx was described as "no longer mounted anywhere", and its own file header said the same. That is not accurate - Play.tsx:1291 still renders `case "mines": return <MinefieldPro isOpen onClose={...} />` in the dialog switch. The branch is not REACHED by a tile click, because ROUTED_GAME_PATHS maps mines to /play/mines first, but it is live code in the tree, not deleted code. More to the point, the file still shipped the ungated selector: GRID_SIZES = [25,36,49,64] with every segment clickable and gridSize forwarded to startMinesGame, i.e. exactly the divergence LIVE_RAIL_GRID_SIZES was created to close, sitting one route-map entry away from being reachable again. MinefieldPro.tsx now imports LIVE_RAIL_GRID_SIZES and applies the same gate and the same per-control reason string as MinesBetPanel, and its header comment now states the real reachability instead of claiming the file is dead. A stale "this is unmounted" note is how a resurrected divergence gets missed. ★ STILL OPEN, not a frame gap: the ADMIN key mines_house_edge (default 0.03) is read by NOTHING on the live rail, so the gaming-config panel is decorative for this game. ★ 2026-08-05 GRID-SIZE GATE VERIFIED IN A BROWSER, not just in source. /play/mines rendered at 1440 and the Grid Size row reports, from the live DOM: 25 enabled; 36 disabled with title '36-tile boards are not supported by the settlement engine yet'; 49 disabled with the matching message; and Custom disabled with 'No custom board sizes are available'. So the control now tells the truth instead of silently no-opping, and the 64-tile path that used to quote a 64-tile ladder against a 25-tile settlement is unreachable from either the segments or Custom. The legacy MinefieldPro dialog (still a live branch in Play.tsx's switch, though the tile routes) was brought to the same gate this pass so a remount cannot resurrect the divergence. ★★★ 2026-08-05 CLOSED. All four remaining partial frames resolve, so the family flips partial -> done. 9163-4859 (desktop page), 9163-5572 (mobile page) and 9003-111181 (tablet B, the shape actually implemented) were each held partial ONLY for standing product rules and deliberate one-implementation choices - the no-mock-data exclusion of Figma's sample rows, the app-wide no-practice-mode rule, the frames' own Dice-art and Dice-title leftovers, two Figma copy defects shipped corrected, and a responsive tablet board rather than a second pixel set. None is outstanding work. 9003-110110 (tablet A) is RE-FILED from partial to deferred: it is a rejected rival that contradicts both tablet B and the mobile frame, so building it would mean un-building B - the same treatment this catalog already gives 9003-118852, 9003-83784, 9003-98680 and 9003-132031. Re-verified in a real browser on /play/mines at 1440: 0 of 10 bet-panel labels missing, 0 of 7 page regions missing, 0 forbidden strings, 0px horizontal overflow, no error boundary. ★ THE PANEL PRINTS THE RAIL AND THE ARITHMETIC CLOSES: Potential Profit renders 1.0795x at the default 3 mines / 25 tiles, and 0.95 x 25/22 = 1.07954..., i.e. the correct first-pick odds at exactly the 5% house edge - the same 95% RTP dice and darts run - computed from live state rather than printed from the frame. [vverify: partial | Rebuilt 347x347 -> 375x369 on 2026-09-10; the match verdict below was measured on 9163-6955 and needs re-measuring. Mobile board verified as the same design at ratio: measured tile 53.453 with gap 5.938 at WIDTH=375, i.e. gap/tile 0.1111 identical to desktop's 11.437/103.047. Same five tile states, same committed art, same BOMB_CROP. Driven by the shared MinesBoard, so it cannot drift from the desktop board.]

column5: CLOSED 2026-08-05: vverify.skratch.tsv now records 9 match / 4 deferred / 0 partial. The two page frames (9003-142707 desktop, 9212-23847 mobile) and the chosen tablet frame (9003-148466) were partial only because /play/scratchers was unwired; Skai-Trading f0c229e1e wired it and all three are now screenshotted end to end on the live route at 1440/768/375. REAL-DATA FIX SHIPPED: the paytable strip's six chips were ordered money·star·slot·trophy·clover·gem, read off the chips' generic node names (Group 295…Group 305) rather than their art. Re-read from the RENDERED strip at all three scales (desktop 9212:21235, tablet 9058:2158, mobile 9212:25292) the designer's order is trophy·money·slot·star·clover·gem at every scale — which is also ascending by the real server multiplier 5·6·12·25·75·250 — so slots 0/1/3 were wrong; corrected in ScratchCardPro.tsx and verified live reading 5x 6x 12x 25x 75x 250x. Figma prints 1.98x on all six chips (one placeholder repeated); the real SCRATCH_PAYOUTS values are shown instead, and 7️⃣/🍒/🔔 pay ZERO by design so they are correctly absent from the strip. SECOND REAL-DATA FIX: the local-dev settlement mock in modules/skai-gaming/src/services/gaming/gameSettlementService.ts carried the RETIRED pre-retune scratch table (💎100 🍀25 ⭐10 🎰5 💰3 🏆2 and 7️⃣1.5 🍒1 🔔0.5) behind a "MUST MATCH edge function" comment, drawn from a UNIFORM 1-in-9 roll and read with `|| 1` — the exact trap paytables.ts warns about, which pays every zero-symbol 1x. Re-synced to the live table + SCRATCH_WEIGHTS with `?? 0`; dev-only path, never reachable in prod. NOTE CORRECTED: 9003-139146 is the AUTO/Advanced-OFF panel, not Manual — the true Manual panel frame is 9058-2367, mis-filed under the hilo section. The 4 deferred are 9003-149392 (the second, NOT-chosen 768 frame), 9220-26119 (region-restriction modal — the app already implements region denial in src/components/auth/GeoRestrictedRoute.tsx and a second competing modal on one concern was declined; copy preserved in scratchersPageContent.ts as SCRATCHERS_REGION_MODAL_DEFERRED) and 9220-26173 / 9220-26174 (pasted reference SCREENSHOTS, not design frames — nothing to implement). ★ RE-FILING RECOMMENDED: three frames currently under section `hilo` are Scratchers' and should move to `skratch` — 9058-1833 (the tablet board: 326 card frame, 3x3 at cell 87.5436 / gap 10.5613, six-across 653 Match-3-to-Win strip; ratios pad/frame 0.06479, gap/cell 0.12064, art/cell 0.67828 are IDENTICAL to the built scratchersTheme.ts BOARD_RATIO), 9058-2367 (the 356x621 MANUAL bet panel) and 9058-5154 (a third Scratchers tablet page, 768x1607, carrying the same Coinflip-panel designer error as 9003-148466/9003-149392). All three are already covered by the shipped responsive components — no new build needed. DECLINED: 9058-4372, whose Figma title also reads "Scratchers", is NOT Scratchers — its board and panel are Hi-Lo's (Profit Higher/Lower, King Being The Highest / Ace Being The Lowest, Higher-or-Same 30.77% / Lower-or-Same 76.92%, Start Card) and its blurb is Hi-Lo's; only its breadcrumb and info-card strings say Scratchers. column5: 9948-24618 / 9948-25380 (the two page frames) AND THE WHOLE SECTION. THIS ROW IS AN ASSESSMENT, NOT A PARITY VERDICT — there is no Limbo UI to compare 14 frames against, so nothing here claims match/partial on a frame. ★★★ CORRECTION 2026-08-19, SAME DAY, THE TREE MOVED UNDER THIS ASSESSMENT AND THREE CLAIMS BELOW WENT STALE WITHIN HOURS — read this before the body. (i) "There is no POINTS path" IS NOW FALSE. supabase/functions/_shared/limbo.ts now exists (LIMBO_EDGE_MUL_BPS 9900, LIMBO_MIN/MAX_TARGET_BPS 10100/10000000, limboWinThreshold, settleLimboRound) and supabase/functions/points-game/index.ts wires it end to end — `play_limbo` at :2136, target parsed and bounds-checked at :5173-5185, settled at :5513-5528. So the rail question this row raised is ANSWERED, and answered in the frames' favour: POINTS settles limbo at a 1% edge, matching the chain and the frames, NOT at Dice's 5%. game-settlement/index.ts still has zero limbo. (ii) THE KEEPER DOC DEFECT IS FIXED — main.go now reads ":314 Limbo: target multiplier in BASIS POINTS, i.e. x10000 (20000 = 2.00x)" and keeps a note recording the old wrong text; the neighbouring Dice line was corrected too. Leaving it listed as an open violation would be actively harmful, which is why it is struck below rather than left standing. (iii) EVERY skai-chain LINE NUMBER IN THIS ROW SHIFTED, because gaming.go and gaming_settle_models.go were edited mid-session: settleLimbo 352 -> :388-410, edgeMulBPS 131 -> :141, the GameLimbo registry row 261 -> :276, HouseEdgeBPS 78 -> :93. gaming.go:48 and keeper :130/:185 are unchanged. The FACTS all re-verified identical; only the offsets moved. Cite by symbol, not by line, in a tree this many lanes are writing to. ALSO NEW AND NOT MINE: modules/skai-gaming/src/components/play/games/instant/limboOdds.ts + limboOdds.test.ts, and modules/skai-gaming/src/assets/games/figma/limbo.webp. STILL ABSENT, which is why this row stays `not-started`: there is no LimboGame.tsx, the `instant` barrel does not export one, there is no route and no Play.tsx registration — so no Limbo FRAME is implemented by anything, and the frame-parity verdict is unchanged even though the backend is now largely built. WHAT I VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED. (a) CLIENT: I could find NO Limbo component, page, tile, route, game-art entry or feature flag anywhere. Swept `src/`, `modules/skai-gaming/src/`, `modules/skai-ui/` and `supabase/functions/` case-insensitively for limbo/Limbo/LIMBO. Both are the 99/chance relation, i.e. a 1% house edge, and BOTH AGREE EXACTLY WITH THE CHAIN: settleLimbo wins iff `scaled < edgeMulBPS * OutcomeScale / target` with `edgeMulBPS = 10000 - HouseEdgeBPS = 9900` (gaming_settle_models.go:131, gaming.go:78), so P(win) = 9900/target — 9900/20000 = 49.5% and 9900/19800 = 50.0000%, to the printed digit. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE KENO RESULT and the contrast is the point: Keno's frames were found printing payouts matching no row of the real server table, so a design's numbers are never a source of truth for money — here they happen to match a rail that exists, and that was CHECKED against gaming_settle_models.go rather than believed. THREE ODDS CAVEATS STILL STAND AND MUST NOT BE BUILT PAST. (1) The desktop frames are INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: they pair Multiplier `2.00` with a label reading "Potential Profit: (1.98x)". Against settleLimbo the payout for target 20000 is exactly 2.00x the stake (profit 1.00x), not 1.98x — the frame appears to apply the 1% edge a second time on the payout after it is already priced into the win chance. The mobile frames do not have this problem (target 1.9800 with 50.0000% is self-consistent). Whichever tier is copied literally decides whether the player is quoted the right number. (2) THE PLATFORM DOES NOT AGREE WITH ITSELF ABOUT HOUSE EDGE ACROSS RAILS, and Limbo would inherit that on day one. The chain sets ONE edge for every game (HouseEdgeBPS = 100, 1%), while the edge-function/POINTS rail for the mechanically identical Dice runs at 95 RTP / 5% — diceOdds.ts:20 `RTP_PERCENT = 95`, with a docblock recording that the client once used "99/winChance (1% edge) which OVERSTATED the pre-roll payout vs settlement". A Limbo widget built to these frames displays 1% odds; a POINTS Limbo settling like Dice would pay 5%-edge odds; the numbers in these frames are only correct for the chain rail. (3) FIXED 2026-08-19, RECORDED HERE ONLY FOR THE LESSON — DO NOT RE-REPORT: cmd/skai-gaming-keeper/main.go used to document the wire param as "Limbo: target multiplier * 100 (e.g., 200 = 2.00x)" while settleLimbo divides by 10000 and MinParam is 10100, i.e. wrong by 100x. For MECHANICS AND MATH: crash is NOT the closest — Dice and Price Grid are. Limbo is not a rising multiplier the player races; it is a SINGLE INSTANT ROLL against a target the player set before pressing the button, with no cash-out, no timer and no round to join. That is exactly Dice (modules/skai-gaming/src/components/play/games/instant/DiceGame.tsx + diceOdds.ts, which already owns the win-chance <-> multiplier <-> threshold <-> Potential Profit conversions and the integer-rail truncation rule for POINTS) and exactly price_grid_settle (supabase/functions/game-settlement/index.ts:13355-13600, `winProbability = (1 / multiplier) * (1 - houseEdge)`, provably-fair roll 0..10000, threshold, max-profit cap, edge read from server config never from bet metadata after IF#1139). GENUINE DIFFERENCE FROM DICE: the display is one giant number plus a history chip rail rather than a slider, and there is no over/under condition. BUILD ESTIMATE, WHAT IS ALREADY THERE. THREE different numbers hide behind "md": the Figma file's own `--rounded-md` is 6px (g-shell, via get_design_context on baccarat 9799:16717, which returns the square as `rounded-[var(--rounded-md,6px)]` with a 1px #123f3c border); the token object says 8px (modules/skai-ui/src/lib/design-tokens.ts:1282 `skaiBorderRadius.md`); and the class actually resolves to 10px, because tailwind-preset.ts:392-397 spreads `skaiBorderRadius` and then OVERWRITES lg/md/sm with `var(--radius)` / `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` / `calc(var(--radius) - 4px)`, and the app sets `--radius: 0.75rem` at src/index.css:539. FRAME DEFECTS TO REPORT UPSTREAM RATHER THAN REPRODUCE: the same 1.58x result is a RED chip in 10004-29705 and a neutral WHITE chip in 10004-29637 after the rail shifts, which implies a third chip state that does not exist; the panels price the bet in SKAI while the Balance row reads "100.11 USDC" and the platform's rails are POINTS/SKAI/sUSD; and "Potential Profit: $1,376.97 / 1376.97 SKAI" on a stake of 1 is placeholder content of the same class as Chicken's fabricated "Total: $89.01", reproducible by no rail and covered by the no-mock-data rule. WHETHER LIMBO SHOULD BE BUILT AT ALL IS CASEY'S CALL AND NOTHING HERE IS A RECOMMENDATION. The facts he needs: the design is 9 real frames and the page half is a copy of a page that already ships; the odds in the frames are real chain odds, not invented; the chain can already settle it; and the reason it would still not be playable on day one is the same reason nothing else settles in sUSD today (the chain money rails are down on an unset service key, and game_history has never recorded a single limbo row).
